newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-SPRINT QUEEN JONES WINS LONG JUMP AT U.S. CHAMPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SPRINT QUEEN JONES WINS LONG JUMP AT U.S. CHAMPS.

text.p: Newly crowned U.S. sprint queen Marion Jones outdueled her idol, Jackie Joyner-Kersee, with the long jump of her life to conclude a sensational week at the U.S. athletics championships on Sunday.
The 21-year-old former college basketball player leaped a a world-leading 6.93 meters (22 feet, 9 inches) to claim her second gold medal of the week.
"I'm overwhelmed," said Jones, who Thursday won the women's 100 meters after producing the year's fastest time of 10.92 seconds the previous night.

"It was a great experience to jump against one of my idols and to come away with a personal best and win the long jump," said the former teenage star who had been away from the sport for almost two years. "It's been a great week."
Joyner-Kersee finished second with a wind-assisted 6.91 meters (22 feet, 8 inches).
The 35-year-old American legend, who is retiring after this season, had taken the lead from Jones with that mark on her fifth attempt. Then Jones delivered, "the jump my life."
The final day of the championships also produced the year's best performances in the men's 400-meter hurdles and the women's 100-meter hurdles.

Bryan Bronson ran down Olympic and world champion Derrick Adkins on the final straight to win the 400-meter hurdles in 47.79 seconds. Adkins claimed silver in 48.00 seconds, the year's second fastest time.
Newcomer Melissa Morrison's lifetime best of 12.61 seconds decided the women's 100-meter hurdles.

World shot put champion John Godina finally made the U.S. world championships team with a lifetime throw of 67.40 meters (221 feet, 1 inch) in the men's discus. Only Germany's Lars Riedel has thrown farther this year.
Godina had missed the U.S. team in the shot by finishing fourth earlier in the week.
Only the top three finishers in each final at the national championship meet qualified for the U.S. team for the August world championships in Athens.
Three other Americans also came close to world-leading performances Sunday.

U.S. record holder Lawrence Johnson cleared 5.90 meters (19 feet, 4 1/4 inches) in the pole vault, Regina Jacobs clocked four minutes, 3.42 seconds in the women's 1,500 meters, and Inger Miller ran 22.62 seconds in the women's 200 meters.
Olympic high jump champion Charles Austin also claimed gold, clearing 2.31 meters (7 feet 7 inches).
